- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above prior peak for next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; re-forecast with 1–2% upward correction after sentiment crossover.
- Model underperforms in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33/1.00); apply smoothing filter or use 14-day moving average for stabilization.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model tends to lag; add 1–2% lag correction for next 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment history shows 3+ consecutive 0.00 values, model often underestimates; apply +2% bias to forecast for next 5 periods.
